summary: LOKI 3PL is an asset-based third-party logistics provider headquartered at 40D Cotters Ln in East Brunswick, NJ, which it describes as the hub of its East Coast operations. It markets warehousing, truckload/LTL freight and multi-channel ecommerce fulfillment (Shopify, Amazon, WooCommerce, TikTok Shop and others) through 11 first-party fulfillment centers in the US and Canada, claiming 2M+ sq ft, 50,000+ pallet positions, a 2 PM same-day cutoff and 98%+ on-time shipping. Lead capture runs on a multi-step quote questionnaire and a general phone/email inbox, and the careers page lists no specific openings, suggesting a small commercial/back-office team relative to the facility footprint it advertises.

facts.fact: Company headquarters is listed as 40D Cotters Ln, East Brunswick, NJ 08816.

The site describes the East Brunswick, NJ facility as 'the heart of East Coast operations' and says LOKI runs 11 first-party fulfillment centers across the US and Canada, every warehouse owned and operated directly with in-house systems and direct employees.
Network scale is stated as 'over 2 million square feet of space' and '50,000+ pallet positions'; orders placed before 2 PM ship the same day, with 98%+ on-time performance and 99.9% order accuracy.

California location page cites '2+ million square feet total', '11 fulfillment centers', '18 dock doors per facility', and proximity 'within 30 miles' of major highways and 'within 60 miles of the ports'.
Services described as asset-based 3PL: transportation, warehousing and multi-channel fulfillment 'with a dedicated fleet of trucks and nationwide coverage'.

Platform integrations listed: Shopify, WooCommerce, BigCommerce, Magento, Amazon, eBay, Walmart Marketplace and Etsy, plus a REST API with webhooks and GraphQL; returns handled with restock/dispose/return decisions and return-reason analytics.

Operations claims on the NJ page include 24/7 customer support, 24/7 operations, '100 to 100,000+ orders per month', month-to-month agreements, no setup fees, and site visits available by appointment.
The FAQ page names warehouses in Edison NJ, Los Angeles and Dallas, and says clients get real-time inventory tracking and integrations with Shopify and Amazon.

Lead intake uses a five-step warehousing quote questionnaire asking company info, job title, whether they own the product, current US warehouse presence, preferred inventory location, max shipping distance, start timing, project type and peak season.

Warehouse quote page promises 'It takes about 60 seconds, and our team will review your requirements and get back to you quickly'; the support page describes a three-step process (submit quote request, discuss quote, get started).
Public contact channels shown site-wide are a toll-free number (1-844-565-4537) and sales@loki3pl.com, with a banner advertising that staff speak Spanish and Mandarin.
A Trustindex widget on the NJ page reports 'Based on 134 reviews' from Google, displayed with 4- and 5-star ratings.
The careers page has no job listings or ATS links, only a 'Tell us about yourself' application prompt and general text about warehousing, transportation and supply chain career paths.

The company publishes an active blog and content library: the blog sitemap shows roughly 40+ posts dated from July 2025 through November 2026, plus a case-study page on 'How to Prepare for Peak Season 2026'.
Founder is described only as a logistics veteran with '10 + years in the logistics industry' who reached the C-suite; no name is given on the page.
A job-board search for 'Loki 3PL' on SimplyHired returned 'We could not find any Loki 3PL jobs'.

operations_signals: Inbound interest is captured by a 5-step online questionnaire plus a separate 60-second warehouse quote form; the site says the team reviews requirements and responds, implying manual triage and human quoting (https://loki3pl.com/3pl-warehousing-quote-questionnaire/, https://loki3pl.com/warehouse-form/)

Only general contact channels are published - a toll-free number (1-844-565-4537) and sales@loki3pl.com - with no online scheduling, instant pricing or chatbot visible on the pages reviewed (https://loki3pl.com/support/)
Two parallel quote funnels for warehousing vs. truckload/LTL, plus separate questionnaires per service, which spreads inbound requests across several forms (https://loki3pl.com/support/)

Advertises 24/7 customer support and 24/7 operations, and multilingual phone support in English, Spanish and Mandarin - shift-based coverage of phones and email (https://loki3pl.com/3pl-fulfillment-center-new-jersey/)
Facility tours are 'by appointment' rather than self-scheduled, another manual coordination step (https://loki3pl.com/3pl-fulfillment-center-new-jersey/)
Service commitments are order-cutoff driven: orders before 2 PM ship same day, so exceptions/expedites create same-day coordination load (https://loki3pl.com/3pl-fulfillment-center-texas/)
Claims capacity of '100 to 100,000+ orders per month' with flexible peak staffing, i.e. volume swings that stress scheduling and support (https://loki3pl.com/3pl-fulfillment-center-new-jersey/)
hiring_signals: Careers page shows no open requisitions and no ATS/Greenhouse/Lever link - just a generic 'Tell us about yourself' form, so hiring runs through an inbox rather than a structured pipeline (https://loki3pl.com/career/)

No LOKI 3PL postings surfaced on SimplyHired ('no Loki 3PL jobs'); Indeed, ZipRecruiter, LinkedIn and Jooble returned HTTP 403 to automated access, so current postings could not be verified (https://www.simplyhired.com/search?q=Loki+3PL)

Site copy emphasizes 'ongoing training, leadership development' and 'flexible staffing for peaks', consistent with high-volume warehouse hiring rather than back-office roles (https://loki3pl.com/career/)
Reviews from truck drivers about fast loading suggest dedicated dock/receiving coordination staff (https://loki3pl.com/3pl-fulfillment-center-new-jersey/)
review_themes: Responsiveness and communication are the dominant praise theme - reviewers repeatedly describe the team as quick to update them and easy to reach (https://loki3pl.com/3pl-fulfillment-center-new-jersey/)
Speed of fulfillment and shipping mentioned often, including faster turnaround on DTC orders after switching (https://loki3pl.com/3pl-fulfillment-center-new-jersey/)
Named individual account contacts appear in reviews, indicating relationship-managed accounts rather than self-service portals (https://loki3pl.com/3pl-fulfillment-center-new-jersey/)
Several short driver-side reviews praise quick loading and friendly dock staff, in English and Spanish (https://loki3pl.com/3pl-fulfillment-center-new-jersey/)
Widget on the company's own page shows 134 Google reviews with only 4- and 5-star icons; no negative themes are visible in that curated feed (https://loki3pl.com/3pl-fulfillment-center-new-jersey/)
tech_footprint: Website runs WordPress with Elementor, Yoast SEO, WPForms, WP Fastest Cache, Autoptimize, ShortPixel image CDN and Google Tag Manager (https://loki3pl.com/)
Social proof and review display handled by a Trustindex widget pulling Google reviews (https://loki3pl.com/3pl-fulfillment-center-new-jersey/)
Marketing includes interactive calculators (cubic-feet calculator, pallet calculator) used as lead magnets (https://loki3pl.com/cubic-feet-calculator/, https://loki3pl.com/pallet-calculator/)
Client integration story is API-first: REST API with webhooks and GraphQL, plus marketplace/ecommerce connectors (https://loki3pl.com/3pl-fulfillment-center-new-jersey/)

Real-time WMS tracking with scan-at-every-step, automated cycle counts and audits is described; no client-facing portal or dashboard is mentioned anywhere reviewed (https://loki3pl.com/3pl-fulfillment-center-new-jersey/)

Content marketing engine is prolific (40+ blog posts, white papers, case study, per-state location pages), which suggests investment in SEO/lead generation over back-office tooling (https://loki3pl.com/blog-post-sitemap.xml)

Location pages are template-driven and contain mismatched copy - the NJ fulfillment-center page opens with Florida-focused text and the CA page mixes NJ references (https://loki3pl.com/3pl-fulfillment-center-new-jersey/, https://loki3pl.com/3pl-fulfillment-center-california/)
growth_signals: Advertises 11 first-party fulfillment centers across the US and Canada and over 2 million square feet, with the East Brunswick NJ hub positioned as the East Coast anchor (https://loki3pl.com/3pl-fulfillment-center-new-jersey/)
Location count is stated as both '11' and '12-location network' on the same page, a sign of fast-changing footprint vs. site updates (https://loki3pl.com/3pl-fulfillment-center-new-jersey/)
Site keeps adding service lines and platform pages - TikTok Shop fulfillment, BigCommerce, WooCommerce, B2B/omnichannel pages added in late 2026 (https://loki3pl.com/page-sitemap.xml)
Publishing cadence is heavy and current (posts through November 2026, including a 2026 peak-season case study), consistent with active demand generation (https://loki3pl.com/blog-post-sitemap.xml)

Claims 30 minutes from the Port of New York and New Jersey and one-day reach to 40% of the US population, targeting importers and East Coast DTC brands (https://loki3pl.com/3pl-fulfillment-center-new-jersey/)
Month-to-month agreements, no setup fees and no cancellation penalties are used as a competitive wedge against larger 3PLs (https://loki3pl.com/3pl-fulfillment-center-new-jersey/)
decision_maker: Unknown - the company's Story page refers only to 'our founder' (10+ years in logistics, former C-suite) without naming anyone, and no owner/GM name appears on the site pages reviewed.

inferences.inference: Quote-to-onboarding is likely a manual bottleneck that an agent could automate.
inferences.reasoning: Two separate multi-step questionnaires, a promise that 'our team will review your requirements,' no instant pricing, and no scheduling tool means each inbound lead is read, qualified and re-keyed by a person before a quote goes out.

inferences.inference: Back-office headcount is probably thin relative to the advertised 11-center / 2M sq ft footprint.
inferences.reasoning: The careers page lists no roles at all, hiring appears to run through a generic web form, and marketing output is high while lead handling and client reporting stay phone/email based - growth has been pushed into SEO and facilities rather than admin tooling.

inferences.inference: Customer communication is person-dependent, which is a service risk as volume grows.
inferences.reasoning: Reviews praise named account contacts and responsiveness rather than a portal or dashboard, and the site never mentions a client portal - so status updates, order exceptions and inventory questions likely flow through individual reps' inboxes and phones.

inferences.inference: The published location count and some page copy are ahead of / behind reality, indicating content QA debt.
inferences.reasoning: The NJ page says both '11 first-party fulfillment centers' and '12-location network', the NJ fulfillment-center page opens with Florida copy, and the CA page mixes NJ references - typical of a fast-scaling site built from templates.

inferences.inference: Public customer voice is probably more positive than representative.
inferences.reasoning: The reviews visible are an embedded Trustindex widget on the company's own page showing only 4- and 5-star entries out of 134 Google reviews; independent review sites (Yelp, Trustpilot, BBB) could not be accessed to check for complaints.

inferences.inference: Driver/dock coordination is a real, daily workload worth automating.
inferences.reasoning: Several short reviews are from carriers praising fast loading, and the site advertises same-day cutoff plus appointment-only facility visits - classic dock scheduling and check-in traffic.

data_gaps: Job postings could not be verified: Indeed, ZipRecruiter, LinkedIn, Jooble and Glassdoor returned HTTP 403 to automated access; SimplyHired showed zero LOKI 3PL listings.

Web search providers were unavailable during this task (Exa rate limit, OpenAI quota) and Bing returned unrelated results, so news coverage, press releases and third-party rankings could not be searched.

BBB, Yelp and Trustpilot pages were blocked or behind consent walls, so independent review counts, ratings and complaint themes are unverified; the only review data seen is the company's own Google-review widget (134 reviews).
No headcount or revenue figures found; company size is inferred only from facility claims.

Square footage for the East Brunswick facility specifically is not stated anywhere reviewed - the only figures are network-wide (2M+ sq ft, 50,000+ pallet positions); the '100,000 sq ft East Brunswick facility' from the mapper note could not be confirmed on the site.
Decision-maker name/title not published on the company site; LinkedIn company page returned HTTP 403.
Hours of operation for the facility are not published; only '24/7 operations' and '24/7 support' claims.
No pricing published; costs and contract terms beyond 'month-to-month, no setup fees' are unknown.
